identificationModule.briefTitle: Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Management Following Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion
identificationModule.officialTitle: Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Management Following Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion (INTEGRAL)

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This randomized study was designed to compare two antithrombotic regimens (long-term half-dose apixaban vs long-term aspirin after 45-days of full-dose apixaban) after successful Watchman implantation.

interventions.name: Half-Dose of novel OAC
interventions.description: Patients randomized to long-term half-dose apixaban (Group hdNOAC) will receive half-dose (2.5mg BID) apixaban monotherapy throughout the study period

interventions.name: Low-dose ASA
interventions.description: In the low-dose ASA group, patients will receive full-dose of apixaban for 45 days followed by the low-dose aspirin
otherNames: Patients randomized to long-term aspirin (Group ASA) will receive full-dose (5mg BID) apixaban for 45 days
followed by aspirin 81-100mg monotherapy throughout the study period.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Composite endpoint of DRT, TE and major bleeding events
primaryOutcomes.description: Composite endpoint of device-related thrombosis, TE and major bleeding events

locations.facility: Texas Cardiac Arrhythmia Institute, St. David's Medical Center
